jobs.title: IT Strategic Vendor Management Sr. Specialist
jobs.jd:
This role assists with IT supplier performance management, software and IT services contract compliance, licensing and consumption oversight, service-level reporting, governance activities, technology risk management, financial tracking, and continuous improvement initiatives. The successful candidate will have experience working with IT software contracts, agreements, and/or IT services, along with strong analytical, communication, and relationship management skills. This position requires the ability to manage competing priorities, perform detailed analysis, and support technology vendor relationships that are critical to secure and reliable business operations.
This position does not provide employment pursuant to the terms of a STEM OPT Training Plan.
Responsibilities
Core Responsibilities
•	Support technology supplier relationships by fostering collaboration among IT, business stakeholders, Supply Chain, Legal, Cybersecurity, and vendor organizations to achieve service and business objectives
•	Monitor IT vendor performance against software and IT services contractual obligations, service level agreements (SLAs), key performance indicators (KPIs), operational level agreements (OLAs), license entitlements, and experience-based measures
•	Develop, analyze, and distribute IT vendor scorecards, service performance reports, trends, and dashboards to support operational and executive governance reviews
•	Coordinate and facilitate IT vendor governance meetings, including agenda development, documentation of decisions and action items, issue tracking, escalation management, and follow-up on commitments
•	Assist in the review and interpretation of IT software contracts, license and subscription agreements, statements of work, amendments, renewals, support and maintenance terms, and service-level schedules to support compliance and alignment with technical and business requirements
•	Track vendor, technology, cybersecurity, compliance, and service-delivery risks, issues, escalations, audit findings, and remediation activities, ensuring timely resolution and communication to stakeholders
•	Analyze IT vendor financial information, software licensing and subscription charges, cloud or consumption-based services, invoices, credits, and contractual adjustments to validate accuracy, entitlement, and contractual compliance
•	Partner with IT product and service owners, Supply Chain, Legal, Cybersecurity and business stakeholders to support technology sourcing, vendor assessments, contract negotiations, renewals, and contract lifecycle management activities
•	Identify opportunities for IT service improvement, software license optimization, demand and consumption management, innovation, automation, and cost optimization through analysis of vendor performance, usage data, and industry practices
•	Prepare executive presentations, briefing materials, and management reports that summarize IT supplier performance, contractual compliance, technology and service risks, financial impacts, achievements, and recommended actions
Qualifications
Required Education/Experience
•	Master's Degree and a minimum of 2 years of relevant work experience or
•	Bachelor's Degree and a minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience or
•	Associate's Degree and a minimum of 4 years of relevant work experience or
•	High School Diploma/GED and a minimum of 5 years of relevant work experience
Preferred Education/Experience
•	Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, Information Technology, Finance or a related field and a minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience in IT vendor management, technology supplier relationship management, IT contract or software asset management, technology procurement, and/or IT financial analysis.
Relevant Work Experience
•	Experience working with technology vendors, software publishers, cloud or SaaS providers, managed service providers (MSPs), IT consulting firms, or other IT service providers, required
•	Experience reviewing or administering IT software contracts, licensing or subscription agreements, statements of work, and/or IT services agreements, required
•	Experience analyzing and interpreting IT service performance metrics, SLAs, KPIs, license or subscription usage, and vendor service reports, preferred
•	Experience preparing executive-level reports, presentations, and management communications, preferred
•	Ability to plan, organize, and lead meetings and translate contractual, business, and technical information for diverse stakeholders, preferred
•	Ability to develop clear contract summaries, governance materials, procedures, and documentation for stakeholders with diverse business and technical backgrounds, preferred
•	Working knowledge of IT contract lifecycle activities, including intake, review, approval, execution, renewal, amendment, termination, and obligation tracking, preferred
•	Familiarity with software licensing models, SaaS subscriptions, maintenance and support terms, cloud consumption, data protection, cybersecurity, and audit requirements, preferred
Skills and Abilities
•	Demonstrated analytical skills
•	Strong written and verbal communication skills
•	Demonstrates excellent judgment and decision making skills
•	Develops and delivers effective presentations
Licenses and Certifications
•	Driver's License Required
Physical Demands
•	Sit or stand to use a keyboard, mouse, and computer for the duration of the workday
•	Ability to read small print and symbols
Additional Physical Demands
•	The selected candidate will be assigned a System Emergency Assignment (i.e., an emergency response role) and will be expected to work non-business hours during emergencies, which may include nights, weekends, and holidays.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Contingent Workforce (Lead CW Program Manager)
jobs.salary: $118,000–$149,000 base depending on state (CA/NY/CT/NJ tier at the top), plus equity
jobs.jd: Instacart says its contingent population has grown and it now needs governance, policy and program infrastructure to match. The hire takes over a newly launched MSP/VMS platform (Beeline + Monument) and turns it into a fully governed, scalable program with clear policies, a trusted supplier network and a compliance-first operating model. First-year goals: move from a new system of record to a working program with governance frameworks, SOPs and clear accountability; get hiring managers to adopt the model through communications, training and enablement; and own the roadmap after launch, including international expansion through a centralized EOR, platform enhancements and better spend reporting. Minimum requirements: 7+ years in program management, operations or workforce management, with a record of building programs from scratch in ambiguous, fast-moving settings, plus experience managing vendor or supplier relationships, ideally in staffing, MSP or VMS. Preferred: hands-on time with Beeline, SAP Fieldglass or Workday; familiarity with employment law, worker classification or SOX; a background in HR or People Ops; and experience with international or EOR programs.
jobs.aiWhyFits: It is a newly launched Beeline platform that needs a governed operating model, which is the work you did as MetLife's Beeline Platform Owner across 35,000+ workers.
jobs.aiGaps: The Greenhouse link redirects to Instacart's general careers page, so I couldn't confirm it is still open; the pay tops out near $149k, and you would need a specific example of building a program from scratch.

jobs.title: HR Director, Global Contingent Workforce
jobs.location: New York, NY (US-based remote allowed; hybrid if within 50 miles of an office)
jobs.jd: Owns the strategy, governance, optimization and execution of the contingent workforce program, covering staff augmentation, independent contractors and SOW engagements across regions and business units. Responsibilities: set and run a multi-year CW strategy and roadmap tied to enterprise workforce planning and total-talent goals; own the full lifecycle from demand planning and intake through onboarding, extensions, tenure monitoring and offboarding; manage CW spend, budgeting, forecasting and rate-card governance, and the performance of MSPs and staffing suppliers; oversee worker classification, co-employment risk, independent-contractor governance and audit readiness; lead the VMS and related workforce technology, including evaluating AI-enabled analytics; build executive dashboards on spend, demand, supplier performance and compliance; and lead the CW team while advising senior leaders. Required: 12+ years in workforce management, CW programs, procurement, MSP programs, TA or HR operations; 7+ years leading enterprise-scale CW programs; hands-on MSP and VMS management; and a bachelor's degree. Preferred: an MBA, CCWP, multinational program experience, and platforms such as SAP Fieldglass, Beeline, VNDLY, Workday or Coupa. Hybrid means at least eight onsite days a month.
jobs.aiWhyFits: This is a director-level owner role for an enterprise CW program in NYC, and it maps closely to your MetLife Beeline, MSP-governance, classification and audit work.
jobs.aiGaps: I saw it only on boards (Built In about a month old, Glassdoor and Indeed) and couldn't open the Workday page; MBA and CCWP are preferred, and you would need to show you have led a CW team directly.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Contingent Workforce

jobs.jd: Leads the strategy, operations and continuous improvement of Zillow Group's contingent workforce program and reports to the Senior Manager of ES&O Programs. The role leads a team covering business partnership, supplier management, systems and program operations. It owns the CW systems roadmap and business requirements, working with Product & Technology and Procurement Systems to strengthen the Beeline and Workday integrations, improve data integrity, and deliver automation and system enhancements. With Finance, Procurement and Strategic Sourcing it sets up financial and supplier processes: invoice reconciliation, issue resolution, supplier performance monitoring and CW spend reporting. It also owns a consistent onboarding, access, support and offboarding experience for each engagement type. Requirements: 7+ years designing, implementing and leading CW programs in complex cross-functional settings, and deep expertise in classification assessments, engagement requirements and program governance, working with Legal and compliance. Preferred: experience moving CW responsibilities from an MSP to an in-house or hybrid model, and expanding programs internationally.
jobs.aiWhyFits: The core asks are owning the Beeline–Workday integration and the supplier-governance roadmap, which is your platform-owner and integrations background.
jobs.aiGaps: Zillow's Workday page was indexed with a 2026-10-29 date, but my fetch didn't show the full posting or an apply button, so I couldn't confirm it is live; the earlier version preferred CCWP and international expansion experience.

jobs.title: Contingent Work Force Manager (JR-202619583)
jobs.location: Remote (Milford, MI hub; 3 days onsite if within commuting radius of a GM hub)
jobs.jd: The single accountable contact linking GM's AV Operations leaders, contingent workers, vendor partners and internal stakeholders. The role builds the operating model, governance and day-to-day support for a vendor-supported contingent workforce at scale. Duties: act as AV Operations' main contact for vendor-managed CW questions and issue resolution; turn workforce demand into requisitions, hiring targets, onboarding plans and readiness actions; coordinate lifecycle events including work-order changes, extensions, transfers and offboarding; triage and track escalations on attendance, timekeeping, onboarding, training and access; monitor vendor staffing progress, service performance and corrective actions with vendor program leadership; build trackers and dashboards on headcount, onboarding status, workforce risks and vendor performance; and work with HR, Legal, IT, Finance, Procurement, Security and EHS on readiness and compliance. Requirements: a bachelor's degree or equivalent; 5+ years in program management, operations, workforce or vendor management, or HR operations; experience supporting a contingent or vendor-managed workforce; and strong metrics and dashboard skills. Responsibilities: develop policies, programs and operating procedures for procurement operations; standardize procurement practice across care settings; analyze operations, find imbalances and recommend cost-effective improvements; set short- and long-range goals for the systems group; review current systems, policies and procedures for accuracy, adequacy and automation potential, and propose changes; develop new programs as procurement grows; run daily operations of the Procurement Information Processing Center, including training and supervising staff and writing procedures and training manuals; periodically assess system capacity and recommend upgrades; and keep vendor relationships current on product developments. Typical requirements across these postings: about 6 years in information processing, program management or systems development, including 3 in a managerial role, plus experience with digital tools that improve supply-chain operations and transparency.
jobs.aiWhyFits: It is a director-level NYC procurement-systems role focused on automation potential, systems capacity and governed procedures, which matches your procurement-systems and controls profile.
jobs.aiGaps: H+H reuses this civil-service title for several different jobs, so confirm which one this listing is on the H+H careers site; it is healthcare supply-chain heavy and I couldn't open an employer page.

jobs.title: Workday Contingent Worker Lead
jobs.jd: Sits on the IT Workforce Management team and reports to the Director, Corporate IT. The role leads technical solution delivery in Workday for hiring, onboarding and offboarding of SPE's contingent workers (anyone not paid through Sony payroll), including development with Workday Extend. Duties: lead the delivery team for Workday CW initiatives with stakeholders across TV and motion-picture productions, Finance, IT and Security; run full-lifecycle delivery of Workday CW product developments, including Extend-based onboarding and offboarding with custom interfaces; define and update Workday configuration and Extend customizations for the CW population; handle user issues on CW management, end-to-end access management and downstream integrations; and support change management through training on CW management, IAM policies and best practices. Requirements: a bachelor's degree in business, IT or a related field; 8+ years as a technology lead in Workday hiring, onboarding and offboarding; Workday Extend certification with 2+ years of build and delivery; and 2+ years managing contingent workers in Workday.
jobs.aiWhyFits: It is a CW technology product-owner role in LA, where your workforce-technology ownership, Workday integrations and offboarding access-termination control are directly relevant.
jobs.aiGaps: Workday Extend certification and 2+ years of Extend build work are listed as must-haves, which you don't have; earlier versions of this posting date back to late 2024, so verify it on Sony's site.

jobs.title: Third Party Risk Management Lead – USDS (Job ID A129141)
jobs.jd: Sits in the US Security & Privacy Governance, Risk and Compliance team and works to reduce third-party and supply-chain risk for compliant USDS JV operations while maturing TPRM capabilities. Responsibilities: lead the full third-party risk lifecycle (intake, due diligence, contracting, ongoing monitoring and exit), aligned to enterprise risk and regulatory requirements; prepare metrics, dashboards and narratives on third-party risk posture, key issues and remediation for senior leaders, governance forums and audit stakeholders; and drive remediation and risk decisions with senior leaders, including risk-acceptance decisions and timely closure of gaps. Minimum: a bachelor's degree or equivalent and 5+ years in information security, risk, privacy or compliance, with significant TPRM program leadership; and hands-on experience designing and running TPRM processes across the lifecycle in a highly regulated environment, including evaluating vendors' technical and procedural controls. Preferred: vendor risk scoring models, KRIs and dashboards, process automation, and scaling TPRM programs in regulated sectors such as financial services.
jobs.aiWhyFits: It targets your 'Vendor Governance / Third-Party Governance Lead' title, and your controls, audit-remediation and executive-dashboard work with Security and TPRM at a regulated insurer is relevant.
jobs.aiGaps: It wants deep information-security TPRM depth (assessing vendors' technical controls), which goes beyond your vendor-governance background; I couldn't confirm it on TikTok's careers site.

jobs.title: Talent Operations
jobs.jd: A talent operations role at an AI cloud and data-center company. It is the key contact for Fluidstack's contingent worker contracts, advising managers on engagement strategy, compliance requirements and best practices, and supports change management and organizational transformation as the company scales. The posting looks for someone who has worked hands-on with contingent workforce programs, from engagement strategy through compliance, and who has run change management or organizational transformation work while bringing affected people along. It also involves building scalable talent operations processes with Legal, Finance and People partners.
jobs.aiWhyFits: It is an NYC role where you would be the go-to authority on contingent worker contracts and compliance at a fast-growing AI company, with change-management scope.
jobs.aiGaps: It is mid-level with lower pay and in-office, and the JD I saw was a partial summary; Fluidstack's Contingent Workforce Manager role above is the stronger fit at the same company.
